title: Looks open, is closed (suppress)
note: Flagged overdue by naive date logic, but a later superior PET/CT explicitly characterized the same nodule as benign. Reconciliation supersedes it and stays silent — no false alarm.

reports.full_text:
EXAM: CT CHEST WITHOUT CONTRAST
DATE: 2024-06-15
HISTORY: 64-year-old with an incidental pulmonary nodule noted on a prior radiograph.

TECHNIQUE: Non-contrast helical CT of the chest.

FINDINGS:
Lungs: An 11 mm solid nodule is noted in the right middle lobe. No cavitation. No additional suspicious nodules. No effusion.
Mediastinum: No adenopathy.
Bones: Unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:
1. Indeterminate 11 mm solid nodule in the right middle lobe. Recommend follow-up CT chest in 3 months to evaluate for interval change.

EXAM: PET/CT SKULL BASE TO MID-THIGH
DATE: 2024-09-22
HISTORY: 64-year-old with an indeterminate right middle lobe pulmonary nodule; evaluate metabolic activity.

TECHNIQUE: Whole-body FDG PET/CT from skull base to mid-thigh following administration of F-18 FDG.

FINDINGS:
There is no hypermetabolic activity corresponding to the previously noted 11 mm right middle lobe nodule. No FDG-avid pulmonary, mediastinal, or hilar disease. No other focal hypermetabolic abnormality.

IMPRESSION:
No hypermetabolic activity corresponding to the previously noted 11 mm right middle lobe nodule; findings favor a benign etiology. No evidence of FDG-avid malignancy.
